name: Miles Landscaping Playbook
label: Landscaping
summary: Sell the season before it starts, turn every one-time cleanup into a recurring contract, and fill winter with snow, lighting and design work. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: Intro
lines: Sell the season before it starts, turn every one-time cleanup into a recurring contract, and fill winter with snow, lighting and design work. Use with the Miles Master Template (deploy logic, ZIP scoring, customer journey).

sections.title: 1. At a glance
lines: Seasonal + recurring (maintenance, lawn programs) + projects (installs, hardscape)
Spring or fall cleanup, or a free property estimate
Lawn treatment programs of about 4–8 applications a year; aeration and overseeding

sections.title: 2. Seasonality by region
lines: Dec–Mar: snow contracts, holiday lighting, design consults
Jun–Aug heat: xeriscape design, irrigation repair
Marketing calendar: publish spring content and open spring booking Jan–Feb; sell snow contracts Oct–Nov for Nov–Mar service.

sections.title: 3. Location signals (add to ZIP score)
lines: Lot size and single-family detached share (bigger lots = bigger tickets).
Income and home value: maintenance contracts and hardscape sell in higher-income ZIPs.
Snowfall days (north) for snow removal add-on.
Drive time and route density: tight routes are the profit lever, so favor clustered ZIPs.

sections.title: 4. Demographics and audiences
lines: Maintenance buyer: dual-income or older homeowners (45–75) who value time; buy on reliability.
Project buyer: 35–60, higher income, staying in the home; buys on design and photos.
Commercial / HOA: multi-year contracts; reliability and scorecards.
Audiences: homeowners in clustered high-income ZIPs; neighbors of current customers (route density); past one-time customers for recurring conversion.

Load with the Audience framework in the Master Template. Emergency segments get no income or homeowner filter and start at 25+; planned segments use the filters below. Ages are starting points: Miles tightens them from closed-won CRM data after 30 booked jobs.
larger lots; route clustering near current customers
Advantage+ on; suggestion 40-65+; geo = route ZIPs
Search: lawn maintenance, lawn care service; observe Homeowners
median >= $120K or home value top third
snowfall days; current maintenance customers first
Exclude in every segment: customers from the last 12 months (except retention campaigns), open leads and estimates, employees, out-of-area ZIPs.

sections.title: 5. Offer stack
lines: Spring or fall cleanup at $[X]; free estimate
First mow free (or $[X] off first month) with a season contract signed by [date]
[10–20]% off when the season is prepaid or booked before [date]
Lawn program, aeration/overseeding, mulch, irrigation, landscape lighting, hardscape
Snow removal season contract (north); holiday lighting install/takedown
Renewal before season with "same crew, same day"; referral credit for neighbors who sign

sections.title: 6. Channels and campaign build
lines: Local SEO: separate pages for spring cleanup, fall cleanup, lawn maintenance, landscape installation, irrigation, hardscaping, and snow removal (north) per real service city.
Search + LSA for "lawn care [city]", "landscaping near me"; negatives: jobs, DIY, mowers, garden center, seeds.
Meta: before/after projects; neighborhood targeting around existing routes; door hangers on the current route.
Every cleanup gets a follow-up quote for recurring maintenance.

sections.title: 7. Triggers Miles watches
lines: Text recurring clients a check-in + review ask

sections.title: 8. After the job and retention
lines: Convert one-time jobs: cleanup customers get a recurring maintenance quote within 48 hrs.
Mid-season check-in text to recurring clients, then honest review ask to everyone (reviews peak at project completion and mid-season).
Renewal sequence 30 days before season; snow customers get early spring renewal.

sections.title: 9. Compliance and watch-outs
lines: Pesticide/fertilizer applications need state licensing; follow state notification rules.
Respect local watering restrictions and noise ordinances in ads and service promises.
Don't oversell capacity in spring; cap new contracts by route capacity.

sections.title: 10. Deploy checklist
lines: ☐ Confirm services (maintenance, lawn programs, hardscape, irrigation, snow, lighting) and licensing
☐ Score ZIPs on lot size, income, HOA density, route clustering, snowfall
☐ Load cleanup, season contract, early-booking, winter offers
☐ Build seasonal service pages, Search + LSA, Meta around routes
☐ Arm spring warm-up, fall, snow and drought triggers
☐ Turn on cleanup-to-recurring follow-up, mid-season check-in, renewal and referral automations

Sources: seasonal demand curve (LandscapeDesk) · lawn programs 4–8 applications (LeadGen Economy) · content windows and mid-season review timing (W3era) · early-booking discounts (Landscaping cost guide)
